canvases.name: Ideas
canvases.purpose: Ideas takes each rough idea of the operator from capture to 1 committed, validated plan, and closes the idea when its feature is merged (G3). It decides when an idea may move to its next state, holds the operator approval gate, and answers worker questions against the approved assumptions, so that no AI plans 2 ideas at once and no task exists outside an approved plan (FR-2, FR-10, FR-12). It does not run tasks (task-execution), land branches or open the feature (integration), or start processes (fleet-runtime).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: It builds a document, the plan, that is validated only at the hand-over event plan-committed (FR-3) and then executed by task-execution: a specification model. It holds the operator approval gate, where an idea goes on only with the operator's approved hash (FR-10, I7): an approver. Decision D2 is open ([define A18]).

ubiquitous_language.definition: The interactive Opus 5.5 agent of 1 feature that clarifies, specifies and plans 1 idea at a time, with a fresh process per phase
1 line in assumptions.md, [confirmed] or [assumed], that the operator approves or revises; also a reversible assumption that the sub-orchestrator records to answer a worker question (understand N11)
The validated plan.yaml of 1 idea: tasks, dependencies, checks, paired judges. No task exists outside a committed plan
spec.md and requirements.yaml of 1 idea. Every requirement cites an approved assumption or an operator answer. It is written only after approval, in the phase specifying (FR-10).
A worker question to the sub-orchestrator of its feature. It ends as an answer, an own assumption, a revise request, or an escalation to the operator
Not a role in fleetd. The word survives only in the preserved mail contract tag [orchestrator re #<id>] (discover N3)

business_decisions: Only code advances an idea. When an idea is captured, the dispatcher starts its sub-orchestrator on the next pass and the idea goes to clarifying; a --direct idea goes to ticketing with no research and no interview (FR-1, FR-2, FR-12).

An idea passes awaiting_approval only when approval.json, written by fleetd, holds the sha256 of the current assumptions.md, and the approve command ran outside every fleet attempt. An approval written by any other process is ignored (FR-10, I7, C5).
The assumptions validator refuses assumptions.md while any item is marked [open]. When the file validates, fleetd requests the operator approval and posts a herdr notification.
While an idea waits on the operator, its lease is paused. After 30 min idle the sub-orchestrator process stops; after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/.

When the assumptions are approved, or revised and approved again, the dispatcher starts a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the next phase. No phase carries a context window into the next (understand N11 keeps the decision rule of the sub-orchestrator).

A plan is committed all-or-nothing, and only after it passes schema, DAG, coverage, profile and citation checks; a plan for a project with no declared fast gate and full gate is refused (FR-3, FR-4). A judgment-kind task without a paired judge task in another session refuses the plan (understand N12).
Every requirement of an idea in in_progress or later is covered by at least 1 task that is not cancelled (I3).

A worker question is a ledger row with an owner, the sub-orchestrator of the feature. On each pass fleetd starts the owner if it is not running, until an answer is recorded; past its time limit the question escalates to needs-you/ (RR-12, discover Q2 for the limit).

The sub-orchestrator answers a question in 1 of 4 ways: cite the approved line, send a revise to the operator, replan the task, or record its own reversible assumption. Only product direction, scope or a trade-off the operator must own goes to the operator (understand N11, design decision D13).
When task-execution asks for a replan, the sub-orchestrator replans the task once; the replanned task goes back to task-execution as task-replanned.
When every task of the idea is landed on its feature branch, the idea goes to integrating. When the feature is merged and every worktree of the idea is removed, the idea goes to merged (discover N4).

Every feature that is not merged and not abandoned has exactly 1 live sub-orchestrator or waits on the operator (I7, I13). The dispatcher starts a missing one and stops an extra one on each pass, through worker-profiles launch-environment and fleet-runtime start-agent-process (connect N3).

canvases.name: Task execution
canvases.purpose: Task execution decides which worker runs each ready task, holds every attempt to an earned lease, and decides from facts on disk when a task is done, so that no task stalls silently (G1) and the subscription usage is used fully (G4). It serves the sub-orchestrator and the operator: they see each task verified done or escalated with a reason. It does not plan tasks (ideas), keep worktrees (worktree-custody), land branches (integration), or build launch environments and start processes (worker-profiles, fleet-runtime).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: It owns the task, attempt and verification aggregates and moves them through state machines with real invariants (I1, I2, I4, I5, RR-2, RR-3). Policies and the clock drive almost all of its 17 commands; the worker, agent CLI and provider pool inputs pass an internal anticorruption layer ([define A15]), not a gateway role.

ubiquitous_language.definition: A planned unit of work from plan.yaml with a kind, a check and an owner path set; it survives many attempts (H1)
1 run of 1 worker on 1 task (A1, A2, ...), launched through the wrapper and ended by fleetd
The time-limited hold of 1 attempt on its task. It renews only on earned activity and pauses during sleep and waiting_quota (discover N1)
The persona that a worker persona names for use when its provider pool shows a usage limit or an outage
A task of kind judge that ranks the misses of 1 judgment-kind task CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW; it needs no judge itself (H5)
A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files
The acceptance command of a task. The verifier runs it in the worktree, in the sandbox profile of the worker
A task state that only the verifier sets, from facts on disk. It does not mean landed or merged (understand N4)
A task state: every dependency is done and the task waits for dispatch (discover N6)
A code kind of a task (with quality, refactor and security). It is not the feature of the integration context (discover N2)

The check of 1 attempt's result that decides done: result.json validates, the task check passes in the worker's sandbox, and the review (code kinds) or the paired judge (judgment kinds) passes. It is the only writer of done.

business_decisions: Only the verifier moves a task to done. A task is done only when result.json exists and validates, and its check passes when fleetd runs it in the worker's sandbox; a code kind also needs today's review scripts to pass, and a judgment kind needs its judge task to report no open CRITICAL item (RR-3, SR-4, understand N4, discover N4).
When a plan is committed, every task whose dependencies are all done becomes ready; no task is ready while a dependency is not done (I2). A refused plan escalates its tasks.

fleetd pushes each ready task to a worker: it leases the task, asks worktree-custody for the worktree, writes task.yaml and inbox/START.md, then launches the attempt. A worker never searches for work (FR-5).

A lease renews only when the process is alive, the wrapper heartbeat is under 30 s old, and activity happened within stall_after (default 300 s). An expired lease ends the attempt; a task never stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1).
Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. A sleep never expires a lease (PL-4).

Stall ladder: idle_no_result gets the constant doorbell once, again 2 min later; still idle or hung ends the attempt with outcome stalled; waiting_approval ends the attempt and marks the profile unhealthy; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result.

A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 ledger transaction before any signal is sent (04 S7). The stop signals only the recorded PID with its start time, and refuses a worker of another host (04 S8).

A usage limit or a provider outage is not a stall and burns no attempt. If the persona's fallback is on another provider, the task restarts at once on the fallback persona in the same worktree; else it waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused until the pool resets (RR-11).
fleetd paces dispatch to each pool's usage window so that the usage is consumed by the reset (OR-4, 06 S13). The target of full use is open (understand Q1).

Any non-verified outcome retries after a backoff of 30 s, 2 min, then 8 min in the same worktree, with a handoff file, while attempts remain under the profile's max_attempts. Then the task goes to its sub-orchestrator for 1 replan, then to needs-you/ (RR-6).
An operator requeue of a held task resets its attempt count (attempt_floor, 04 L8). A task parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree and its dependents stay blocked (04 L5 with integration).
No 2 running tasks of 1 feature own overlapping paths, and an exclusive task runs alone (04 L6).

A judge verdict with an open CRITICAL item opens a fix in a fresh session; after 2 fix rounds with a CRITICAL item left, the task escalates to the operator. A HIGH finding goes to the sub-orchestrator to fix or dismiss. A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW item (FR-4, FM-33, discover N5).
A worker that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write the result; the wrapper does this, not the model.

When a question is answered, or the sub-orchestrator records its own assumption, the parked task resumes its worker session with the answer; if the resume fails, a fresh worker starts from the question, the answer and the committed work (RR-12).
A failed rescue of the task's worktree escalates the task; nothing is removed (RR-9). A task branch that conflicts on landing goes back to the same worker.
No worker runs more than 1 attempt at a time (I4). Every live pane and process under the fleet belongs to a live attempt; anything else is stopped (I5).

Every launch asks worker-profiles for the launch environment and calls fleet-runtime start-agent-process; this context never builds an environment or starts a process itself (connect N3, decompose N2). No process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4).

canvases.purpose: Worktree custody owns every worktree from the moment it is reserved to the moment it is removed, so that no work a worker paid for is lost (G2). It decides when a worktree may be created, reused, rescued or removed, and it reconciles the ledger, the work directory and git on every pass. It serves task-execution, which gets a worktree for each leased task. It does not land or delete branches (integration) and does not decide task states (task-execution).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: It owns the worktree aggregate, whose lifecycle (reserved, created, landing, landed, orphaned, removed) protects invariant I6 and rescue rule RR-9. The clock and policies drive its 4 commands; no person commands it.

ubiquitous_language.definition: The git working tree that fleetd leases to 1 task before it exists and never removes before its work is landed or rescued
A verified commit under refs/horch/rescue/ that saves the full state of a tree or an old branch tip before cleanup or rebase
Same as Lease in this context: the worktree row that holds 1 worktree for 1 task and 1 owner. It is not the attempt lease of task-execution (decompose N4).
A worktree, on disk or in git worktree list, that the ledger does not own or whose owner attempt is dead. It is adopted or rescued, never deleted.

A worktree state: nothing in the worktree is unique any more, so fleetd may remove it (discover N6)

business_decisions: A worktree row is written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. Only fleetd creates or removes worktrees (FR-11). A row left in reserved by a crash is created or dropped on the next pass.

No worktree is removed until its commits, its uncommitted files and its untracked files are saved on a rescue ref under refs/horch/rescue/, and that ref is read back and shown to hold them (RR-9). A rescue that fails verification leaves the tree in place and escalates the task.

Every pass compares the ledger with the work directory, and git worktree list every 60 s. A worktree on disk with no row, or with no live owner attempt, is adopted or rescued within 1 pass and never deleted (RR-10, I6).
Drop and cleanup refuse a dirty tree, a branch with a git stash entry, unpublished unique commits, and a HEAD that moved during the checks (04 W6).

Archive and trash refs only move forward, each ref write is read back before a folder is removed, and trash refs expire after 30 days (04 W8). Triage commits modified and untracked files before ARCHIVE or DELETE (04 W9).

A worktree survives attempts: a retry, a fallback restart or a resume reuses the same worktree (understand N1). The worktree goes to landing when its task branch is verified and to landed when the branch landed; only a landed or rescued worktree is removed (decompose N6).
An abandoned task branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued is recorded (connect N4). No git call runs inside a ledger transaction.

canvases.name: Landing and integration
canvases.purpose: Integration decides when verified task branches land on their feature branch and when a feature is ready for its pull request, so that each idea reaches the primary branch through its own feature (G3) and no landing overwrites other work (G2). It serves the operator, who merges 1 tested pull request per feature, and the sub-orchestrator, which gets conflicts as resolver tasks. It finds conflicts between features early by trial merges and keeps each feature branch rebased. It does not verify tasks (task-execution) and does not remove worktrees (worktree-custody).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: It owns the task-branch and feature aggregates and the land lock, with state machines and the no-loss invariants I8 to I12. Only fleetd code and 2 operator commands act here; git and GitHub pass an internal anticorruption layer ([define A15]).

business_decisions: A feature opens when its sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions, or when fleetd accepts a --direct idea; it gets 1 feature branch from the primary branch (understand N2, discover N2).

A task branch becomes ready only when its task is done (verified). Several ready task branches of 1 feature form 1 bundle on the feature branch tip in queue order; the fast gate runs once on it. No human approves a landing on a feature branch.

On a fast gate pass, the feature branch moves forward to the bundle by fast-forward only (I9). On a failure, fleetd bisects the bundle; the failing task branch goes to gate_failed and its triage task goes to the sub-orchestrator.
Under the land lock (1 h, 5 tries), just before the fast-forward, fleetd checks that the task is still landing and held by its worker; a cancelled task lands nothing (04 F9).
A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7). A passed step stands only for the tree it judged; new commits reopen the land and every later step (04 F5).
Every git network call has a wall-clock bound: push 10 min, others 3 min, and it never retries (04 F11).
A task is landed, and a feature is merged, only when its changes are in the target branch by content, also after a squash merge (I8). Merged is read from git, not from the GitHub API ([define A19]).

Before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists (I10). A fleet branch with no ledger row is adopted as an orphan row and reported, never deleted (I11). A branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it (I12).

When a feature tip or the primary branch moves, fleetd trial-merges each in-flight feature against the primary branch and every other in-flight feature with git merge-tree, no checkout. A conflict stacks the younger feature on the older one and opens 1 resolver task of at most 100 changed lines or 2 files (understand Q7).
When the primary branch moves, each feature branch rebases, bottom of a stack first, and the fast gate runs again; a rebase conflict opens a resolver task.
When every task of an idea is landed, the full gate runs on the feature tip over the current primary branch. A pass goes stale when either tip moves. A failure opens triage tasks of the feature.
A feature is ready only with a current full gate pass. Then its pull request opens: with pr gh through GitHub, with pr manual by a push and the compare URL. The operator merges by default.
A task branch parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree, and unlanded work stays listed for a decision; a finding is decided once (04 L5, L9).
An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator; a rescue ref is kept, and the branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued (connect N4).

canvases.purpose: Worker profiles turns 1 named worker profile into the exact CLI, flags, environment, config files and sandbox of each agent launch, so that every agent runs on the operator's subscription logins and never with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (C2). It serves ideas and task-execution, which ask it for a launch environment before every launch. It keeps the adapters of every agent CLI correct by docs sync and conformance tests, and marks a profile unhealthy when its adapter fails. It does not start processes (fleet-runtime) and does not choose which task runs (task-execution).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: Every launch of every context passes through its launch-environment query, which applies the environment scrub and the login rules (decompose N2, connect N3). It ensures that other contexts carry out the operator's credential rule: an enforcer. It owns 1 aggregate, the worker profile, with few commands.

agy children lose GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL, and the roster rejects them (06 S3). Secrets reach agents only through env vars that the profile names, never through task files (SR-2).

A profile must declare CLI, model, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, context budget, timeouts and restart policy, and every worker persona must name a fallback persona; the roster refuses an incomplete profile (FR-6).
A sandboxed persona does not start on a host that cannot sandbox it (06 S9). Each worker writes only to its task directory, its worktree and the paths its profile names (SR-1).

When an adapter conformance test fails, its profile is marked unhealthy, and dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile until a conformance test passes. A waiting_approval stall also marks the profile unhealthy.

The private CODEX_HOME links every entry of the real codex home except rules/, the Prime agent dir links auth.json, and every codex launch gets --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (06 S4, S5, S6). Trust writes stay narrow (06 S10).

Each agent runs with a context limit of 256k tokens, set through the CLI's own setting where one exists; else the wrapper ends the attempt with a handoff at 256k (FR-9). The OpenCode, pi and Prime adapters carry over (06 S15).

canvases.name: Fleet runtime
canvases.purpose: Fleet runtime keeps fleetd alive and current on macOS, Linux and Windows, so that supervision never stops silently and no work is lost on a restart (G1, G2). It provides every other context with the single ledger writer, the command channel, the platform layer and the start of agent processes. It decides when fleetd is hung or old and restarts it. It does not decide the rows of other contexts' tables (organise N2) or any task, idea, worktree or branch state.
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: It wraps the OS service managers, herdr and the OS process and file facts behind 1 platform interface, and translates them for core code: a gateway. It also executes the daemon lifecycle (heartbeat, hang restart, binary restart, schema migration): an execution context with no domain aggregate.

ubiquitous_language.definition: The supervised daemon role of the horch binary (horch fleetd): the only ledger writer, which runs the reconcile pass of all 6 contexts every 5 s (organise N1).
The time of fleetd's last full pass, written after each pass. horch fleetd check reads it. It is not the wrapper heartbeat.json of an attempt.

1 interface with 1 module per OS for service install and restart, hang detection, process facts, process group stop, file watching, sandboxing, sleep and wake, the command channel transport and the machine probe (PL-2).
The local transport on which CLI commands and agents send requests to fleetd. fleetd validates each request and writes the result to the ledger.
The SQLite file ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3 in WAL mode: an event log plus derived tables. Only fleetd writes it; each context owns its own tables (understand N17, organise N2).
horch fleetd check: the heartbeat check that restarts fleetd when its last full pass is older than 30 s of awake time. It is not a task check
The fleet-runtime call that starts the fleet-run wrapper of 1 attempt, or 1 sub-orchestrator pane through the herdr adapter, in its own process group. Coined in connect (assumption A6)

business_decisions: Exactly 1 process, fleetd, writes the ledger; every other process opens it read-only and sends requests on the command channel or writes files (RR-5, C4, understand N5). Each context still decides the rows of its own tables (organise N2, decompose N5).

fleetd writes a heartbeat after each full pass. When the heartbeat is older than 30 s of awake time, horch fleetd check restarts the service; on Linux the systemd watchdog does it. Every horch CLI command makes the same check before it sends its request (PL-5).
When the horch binary changes, fleetd restarts on the new binary at once; a CLI that finds an older daemon restarts it. The control loop exits only between passes (OR-6, 04 S10, 04 S7).
Schema migration is forward-only at daemon start: a backup is written first and 3 are kept, a newer schema is refused, and a development build does not migrate the shared ledger (OR-6, C4).
Core fleetd code has no OS cfg. It calls 1 platform interface with 1 module per OS; an OS without an equivalent returns an explicit not-supported value that core code decides on (PL-2, PL-3).

New dispatch pauses only while free disk or machine load is past a safety floor, and resumes by itself. A probe that returns unknown (Windows today, 06 S12) is reported, never read as healthy or unhealthy (OR-5).
Mail and outbox directories are mode 0700 and files 0600; a directory that another user owns or can write is refused (04 M5). All protocol file writes are atomic (RR-8).
The only bytes typed into a terminal are 1 fixed doorbell line from fleetd's code (FR-7, C11). horch warns when herdr resume_agents_on_restore is not false (06 S2).

start-agent-process starts each process in its own process group or job object and runs no process start inside a ledger transaction (connect N4). After a herdr restart, fleetd rebuilds from the ledger and the files (C14).
Worker reports reach fleetd as files, not through the Unix-socket channel relay or report socket, so Windows loses no report (06 S11).

[discover A3] Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are cross-cutting. They sit at the end of the executing phase (sequence 540 to 580, before Task Done) because they act on running attempts. Decision D2 records the alternatives. (confidence medium)

[discover A4] fleetd components (idea dispatcher, verifier, landing, wrapper, reconciler) are our own system, not actors. Their commands have actor null and are issued by policies, or have the clock as actor when the reconcile pass fires them. No 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3). (confidence high)
[discover A9] The fleetd command channel, request files while fleetd is down, and the herdr pane mapping are design-level transport; they are not on the board. (confidence medium)
[decompose A6] The ledger is infrastructure that fleet-runtime owns as the single writer. Each context owns the state transitions of its own aggregates; it is not a shared kernel. (confidence medium)

[strategize A1] Ideas is classified supporting, not core (decision D1 is open). Its 24 events are the transitions of 1 fixed idea state machine; the judgment work (research, interview, assumptions, spec, plan) is done by the sub-orchestrator model, not by fleetd code. Scored diff 6, cplx 5. (confidence medium)

[strategize A3] The 2 cores use domain-model: state rows are the truth, and the events table is the audit trail that the one door writes beside each row in the same transaction (design, Ledger, rule 1 One door). Decision D2 keeps the event-sourced reading open. (confidence medium)

[strategize A4] Fleet runtime is supporting, not generic. Its pane hosting (herdr) and host services (launchd, systemd, Windows service) are adopted and only wrapped, as understand N14 says. The single ledger writer, the command channel and the platform layer interface have no product to buy, so the subdomain as a whole is built. (confidence high)

[strategize A7] Every subdomain has evolution custom: each has at least 1 custom capability. The commodity and product capabilities of fleet-runtime (host services, pane hosting) are adopted systems, not built parts. (confidence high)

[connect A1] All 6 contexts run in the 1 fleetd process, so every context-to-context message is in-process. Only the command channel, the file protocol, the herdr adapter, the platform layer, git and GitHub cross a process boundary (design: Architecture and roles). (confidence high)

[connect A2] Cross-context events are in-memory events consumed in the level-triggered 5 s reconcile pass, which re-derives work from ledger rows, so a lost event is caught on the next pass. Delivery is at-least-once and every consumer is idempotent on a natural key (design: Supervision, liveness and reconciliation; decision D1). (confidence high)
[connect A3] Every state change in every flow commits through the single ledger writer in fleet-runtime (decompose N5). The flows do not draw that call on each step. (confidence high)

[connect A4] Operator commands travel as horch CLI requests over the fleetd command channel (Unix socket or named pipe), drawn as via other. When fleetd is down the request goes to a file that fleetd reads at start (design: The command channel). (confidence high)

[organise A2] 1 deployable unit, the horch binary, holds all 6 contexts as modules inside horch-core. The design settles it: fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI and the daemon cannot have different versions (design: Amendments D9, Migration plan, FM-34; understand C1, N6; decompose N1). Decision D1 records the options. (confidence high)

Structural: count of processes other than fleetd that open the ledger for writing, and count of OS cfg sites in core fleetd code (RR-5, PL-2). Target 0.

[connect Q1] Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper: task-execution, worker-profiles or fleet-runtime (decision D2)?

quality_attributes.requirement: A task reaches done only from the verifier, from facts on disk (RR-3).
quality_attributes.scenario: When a worker writes done in its transcript but leaves no valid result.json, then the task stays not-done and the attempt ends as no_result within 1 pass (5 s).

quality_attributes.requirement: A stalled worker loses its lease and its task is retried or escalated; no task stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1).
quality_attributes.scenario: When a worker process is stopped with kill -STOP during an attempt, then the alarm fires within 1 lease (120 s after stall_after) and the task is retried or escalated.

quality_attributes.requirement: A restart of fleetd loses and duplicates no task (RR-7, 04 S7).
quality_attributes.scenario: When fleetd is killed in the middle of a reap, then after restart the attempt is ended and the task requeued exactly once, and outcomes equal a clean run.

quality_attributes.requirement: A usage limit burns no attempt; the task moves to the fallback persona or waits in waiting_quota (RR-11).
quality_attributes.scenario: When a worker's pool reports a usage limit, then its attempt count does not change and the task restarts on the fallback persona at once or waits until the pool resets.

quality_attributes.requirement: No branch moves except by fast-forward to a gated candidate, and no branch is deleted unless landed, merged or rescued (I9, I10, I12).
quality_attributes.scenario: When a bundle fails the fast gate after a rebase, then the feature branch stays at its old tip, the branch resets to its tip from before the land (04 F7), and a rescue ref of the old tip exists.

quality_attributes.requirement: Landed and merged are read from git by content, also for a squash merge (I8).
quality_attributes.scenario: When the operator squash-merges a feature's pull request, then on the next pass the feature becomes merged and its ideas close only after every worktree is removed.

quality_attributes.requirement: A stalled git network call never holds the land lock for longer than its bound (04 F11).
quality_attributes.scenario: When a git push stalls on the network, then it ends at 10 min (other calls at 3 min), is not retried, and the land lock is free for the next bundle.

quality_attributes.requirement: No worktree is removed before its work is landed or on a verified rescue ref (RR-9, I6).
quality_attributes.scenario: When a worker is killed with dirty and untracked files, then after cleanup the rescue ref holds every file, read back before removal.

quality_attributes.requirement: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY never reaches a child process (C2, 05 E-10, 06 S1).
quality_attributes.scenario: When the operator's shell has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set and fleetd launches an attempt, a sub-orchestrator pane, a probe or an updater, then no child environment holds the key.

quality_attributes.requirement: A hung fleetd is restarted on all 3 OSes (PL-5).
quality_attributes.scenario: When fleetd hangs on macOS, Linux or Windows, then the heartbeat check restarts it within 60 s of awake time and the next pass continues from the ledger.

quality_attributes.requirement: Core fleetd code has no OS cfg; a missing OS equivalent returns not-supported (PL-2, PL-3).
quality_attributes.scenario: When the Windows machine probe returns unknown, then dispatch reports it and neither pauses nor treats it as healthy.

quality_attributes.requirement: Only the operator approves an idea's assumptions (FR-10, I7, C5).
quality_attributes.scenario: When a sub-orchestrator writes approval.json or runs horch idea approve, then the idea stays in awaiting_approval and fleetd ignores the file.

notes_for_downstream.text: Sharpens understand N4 and discover N4: task-execution owns exactly 1 writer of the task state done, the verification module. ddd-code must give no other code path (wrapper, worker file, CLI command) a way to set done; a test proves that a result file alone leaves the task in verifying (RR-3).

Each canvas lists its invariants by id (I1 to I13) and its preservation rows by id. ddd-code must turn each listed invariant into 1 check of check_invariants and 1 test in the owning module: task-execution I1, I2, I4, I5; ideas I3, I7, I13; worktree-custody I6; integration I8 to I12. For the active-record contexts the tests are invariant tests with no aggregate (strategize N2): the approval hash (I7) in ideas, the rescue ref before removal (RR-9) in worktree-custody, and the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub in worker-profiles.

Quality attributes of the core contexts are fault-injection scenarios of the design (FM rows). ddd-code must name a test for each quality_attributes row with priority high before the implementation plan names a module.

Confirms and sharpens decompose N3, discover N8 and understand N15: the business_decisions of each canvas cite its preservation rows by id, and each row has exactly 1 owning canvas. 04 L5 is cited by task-execution (the parked task) and integration (the unlanded branch); integration owns it, as decompose N3 says. ddd-code must give each row 1 test in its owning module.

decisions.question: Which business model fits the 2 core contexts, task-execution and integration?

options.summary: cost-reducer: they save operator time and paid usage that today is lost to stalls and lost work.
pros: Matches G1, G2 and G4, which count lost time, lost work and unused usage
fleetd is a tool of 1 team and earns no money
cons: Hides that task-execution produces the output that the operator wants
risks: A reviewer reads cost-reducer as low priority and starves a core context

options.summary: revenue-generator (the pre-fill suggestion): they produce the work output that is the purpose of the fleet.
pros: Shows that these 2 contexts make the value of the fleet
cons: No revenue exists; the label is false for a personal tool
risks: The label invites revenue metrics that the goals do not have

options.summary: engagement-creator: they keep the operator using the fleet by making the work reliable.
pros: Ties to the value proposition: rough ideas in, merged work out
risks: Metrics drift to usage counts instead of no lost work

decisions.rationale: Recommendation A. The goals measure lost time, lost work and unused usage, which is the shape of a cost-reducer. Strongest argument against: the core contexts produce the output of the fleet, and B says that more directly.
would_flip_if: The operator counts merged features per week as the main goal of the fleet
fleetd becomes a product that friends pay for

decisions.question: Which domain role fits the ideas context?

options.summary: specification-model plus approver: ideas builds the plan that task-execution executes, and it holds the operator approval gate.
pros: The plan is a specification that is validated only at the hand-over event plan-committed (FR-3)
The approval gate (FR-10, I7) is an approver behavior
risks: The worker question flow (RR-12) is execution behavior and does not fit either role

options.summary: execution-context (the pre-fill suggestion): ideas tracks each idea through a fixed state machine.
pros: The idea state machine is a real execution with invariants I3, I7, I13
cons: Hides that the plan is a draft until it validates
risks: ddd-code builds rich aggregates where a validated document is enough

options.summary: approver alone: ideas decides if an idea may progress (assumptions approved, plan valid).
cons: Ignores that ideas writes the plan, spec and questions
risks: The question flow has no home in the role

decisions.rationale: Recommendation A. The plan is drafted, validated at 1 hand-over and then executed elsewhere, which is the specification-model heuristic; the approval gate is the approver heuristic. Strongest argument against: the idea state machine and the question flow are execution behavior, so B is also defensible.
would_flip_if: The question flow moves to task-execution (decompose decision D2)
The plan can change after plan-committed without a replan
The approval gate moves out of ideas

plain_words.what: This step wrote 1 page for each of the 6 parts of fleetd. Each page says what the part decides, who it talks to, its words, its rules and how to measure it.
plain_words.decided: Only the verifier says a task is done. Only fleetd writes the ledger. No worktree or branch is deleted before its work is saved. Every agent launch goes through 1 place that removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
plain_words.assumed: We guessed the business label of each part: fleetd earns no money, so most parts save cost. We guessed that ideas writes a plan and approves it, more than it runs work. Both are open for the operator.
plain_words.riskiest: The rules come from the design, so they are safe. The riskiest part is the GitHub and herdr links: no earlier step gave them messages, so we added 2 GitHub rows by hand and asked the connect step to confirm.
